newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Taleban minister sets terms for Afghan pipeline.
newsitem.headline: Taleban minister sets terms for Afghan pipeline.

text.p: Afghanistan's Islamic Taleban movement said on Monday that it would award a multi-million dollar natural gas pipeline to the consortium that could start construction first and offer the most concessions.

"We have made clear that whoever gives greater concessions to Afghanistan and gives the earliest start date will get the opportunity to build the pipeline." Maulawi Ahmedjan, acting Minister of Mines and Industry, told Reuters.
The fundamentalist Taleban overran Kabul last September and control three quarters of the country.

Unocal of the United States in collaboration with Delta Oil of Saudi Arabia, and Bridas of Argentina have shown interest in building the $2.5 billion gas line between Turkmenistan and Pakistan via Afghanistan.
Ahmedjan told Reuters that no decision had been made between the two, but said that a protocol had been signed with Bridas last year.

"We have had discussions with both sides, but so far no agreement has been reached. Bridas signed a protocol in (the southern Afghan Taleban stronghold of) Kandahar when the proposed pipe line route was not fully under Taleban control.
"It was signed on the basis that whatever was beneficial for Afghanistan, the Taleban would support." he said.

He said that the Taleban were looking for the winning contractor to help Afghanistan in its search for oil and gas on its territory as well as providing infrastructural development such as roads and gas link for the towns on the pipeline route.
According to Ahmedjan, in discussions the two competitors had shown different priorities.

"We have spoken to both sides. Unocal said it would consider starting the practical work when there was peace in Afghanistan. Bridas said that they have seen the route, and since there is peace in the areas of the proposed route, they would like to start work." said Ahmedjan.
Ahmedjan said that he believed that work would start soon.
"We think that one of them will start work soon, or maybe both in a joint venture. That is an option that we would prefer. There could even be a third company," he said.
Both Bridas and Unocal have recently sent representatives to Kabul to discuss the project with the Taleban authorities.
A Bridas representative is currently in Kabul, and is in the process of setting up an office in the city.
